Set up your phone for tracing

A steady camera and a well-lit sheet of paper make it easier to follow an outline on your screen.

Set the height and angle

  1. Place your paper on a firm table. Use low-tack tape on two corners if the sheet slides when your hand moves.
  2. Secure your phone in an overhead stand with the rear camera facing the page. Keep the screen parallel to the table. Leave space for your hand and make sure the clamp clears the camera lens.
  3. Open Trace Studio and choose Enable camera. Raise the stand if the paper corners disappear from the preview or the pencil looks blurry. Use the app’s Size control to adjust the drawing once the camera is in position.
  4. Add light from the side opposite your drawing hand. Move the lamp sideways if your hand or the phone casts a shadow across the work.

Check alignment before you start

Turn on Grid and rotate the overlay until it lines up with the edges of the paper. Then lock the overlay. With a light pencil, mark two widely spaced points, such as the top of a head and the bottom of a foot. Check them against the screen after you rest your hand on the table. If both have shifted, move the overlay back into place before tracing the outline.

Keep the physical setup still. Locking holds the drawing in place on the screen. If the phone or paper moves, use the two pencil marks to realign it.

Fix the three most common problems

  • The page looks wider at one end. Level the phone. Tilting the lens makes the far side of the page look narrower.
  • Your pencil line is hard to see. Reduce overlay opacity or choose a line color that contrasts with the pencil. Use Hide to check the marks you’ve already drawn.
  • The camera preview is soft. Raise the phone a little and give the camera time to refocus. A side lamp can help if the room is dim.
